tip_mechanisms.name: Ross-Hime Omni-Wrist III
tip_mechanisms.mechanism: Parallel spherical linkage (repeated identical linkages, preloaded bearings, no gears), driven by 2 linear actuators via cranks; constant-velocity-like pointing
tip_mechanisms.notable_examples: Omni-Wrist III (18 lb, 5 lb payload at 0.02deg resolution); NASA/DTIC laser-comm and sensor pointing
tip_mechanisms.fdm_printable_notes: Linkage is all revolute joints - printable at hobby scale with bearings/pins, but needs tight tolerances and many small bearings; large part count (4 legs). Through-hole fits fan wiring.

tip_mechanisms.mechanism: Four-linkage parallel gimbal with tapered roller bearings, 2 actuators (linear or direct-drive rotary)
tip_mechanisms.notable_examples: Sensor/antenna pointing, laser welding; heavy payload (45 lb with linear actuators)
tip_mechanisms.fdm_printable_notes: Same caveats as Omni-Wrist III; four linkages with heavy bearings - a scaled printed version is possible but part-count heavy.

sources.title: Omni-Wrist VI product page
sources.what_it_supports: +/-90deg pitch/yaw, 2-actuator drive, 'elimination of singularity or key hole' claim

tip_mechanisms.name: Rosheim compact double-gimbal (CV-style) wrist
tip_mechanisms.mechanism: Two gimbal assemblies in a housing (pitch, yaw) with spur gears, each gimbal takes about half the deflection; separate roll drive shaft passes through
tip_mechanisms.range_deg: up to ~180deg pitch/yaw total; roll 360deg continuous
tip_mechanisms.notable_examples: US 4,686,866 (Rosheim, 1987, assigned to Ross-Hime); ancestor of the Omni-Wrist family
tip_mechanisms.fdm_printable_notes: Two pushrods with ball ends drive pitch/yaw - very servo-friendly; double U-joint/spur-gear coupling printable in PETG/nylon. Roll shaft through-center can carry a fan-yaw axis.

tip_mechanisms.name: Milenkovic two-axis non-singular CV wrist (RU + RSR Clemens linkage)
tip_mechanisms.mechanism: RU chain + RSR Clemens linkage in parallel; pointer constrained to spherical motion, roll slaved as constant-velocity; pitch via 4-bar angle doubler
tip_mechanisms.fdm_printable_notes: Pushrod or drum driven; all revolute/spherical joints; 4-bar angle reducer lets a 100deg crank give 200deg pitch - good fit for 180deg-limited hobby servos.

sources.what_it_supports: Mechanism, +/-100deg range, singularity-free claim, 2 actuators

tip_mechanisms.name: Duta-Stanisic dextrous spherical wrist (semicircular-link)
tip_mechanisms.mechanism: Redundant spherical linkage of four semicircular links on a central link with sliding blocks; one arm per hemisphere
tip_mechanisms.range_deg: Near full sphere (any relative motion except arm through arm); no numeric range given
tip_mechanisms.fdm_printable_notes: Curved sliding blocks on printed arcs suffer friction/wear in FDM; better as a concept than a garage build.

sources.title: US4878393A Dextrous spherical robot wrist

tip_mechanisms.name: Ball Drive: sphere driven by 3 omni-wheels (inverse ballbot / Atlas)
tip_mechanisms.mechanism: Output sphere held in a cage and rotated by three omni-wheels pressed on it; constant Jacobian from wheel speeds to sphere angular velocity
tip_mechanisms.range_deg: Unlimited rotation of the sphere itself; usable output-shaft tilt limited by cage opening (typically <= +/-60-90deg)
tip_mechanisms.notable_examples: Atlas motion-simulator sphere (Carleton); CMU Ballbot inverse mouse-ball drive (2006)
tip_mechanisms.fdm_printable_notes: Omni-wheels and the sphere are printable (TPU rollers); slip under load and preload springs are the main issues; continuous-rotation servos or small geared motors with encoders needed. Mass of sphere+3 drives at a tentacle tip is a concern.

sources.title: Weiss, Langlois, Hayes - Unified treatment of the kinematic interface between a sphere and omnidirectional wheel actuators (J. Mech. Robotics 2011)
sources.what_it_supports: 3 wheels needed for 3-DOF; slip notes; singular elevation angles for some wheel layouts

tip_mechanisms.singularity_note: Kinematically singularity-free with 3 well-placed wheels; Carleton paper reports singular elevation angles (0, +/-90deg) for its specific wheel geometry.

tip_mechanisms.range_deg: Large; tilt limited by output-shaft interference (no figure in article)
tip_mechanisms.fdm_printable_notes: Original parts SLA/PEEK; community Thingiverse remix exists. FDM tooth accuracy on spherical gears is marginal - expect backlash.

tip_mechanisms.fdm_printable_notes: Easiest to print; singular (keyhole) when the outer-axis-aligned direction is commanded - fan pointing along pan axis needs fast pan slew.

tip_mechanisms.name: Bevel-gear differential wrist (2 servos, 2 DOF)
tip_mechanisms.mechanism: Two input bevel gears mesh with one output bevel; same-direction input = pitch, opposite = roll/yaw
tip_mechanisms.notable_examples: PCrnjak differential robot wrist (Printables 918284); CN112894783A 2-DOF differential joint module
tip_mechanisms.fdm_printable_notes: Very printable; both motors sit proximal (both servo torques add on each axis). Bevel teeth in PETG/nylon OK; backlash from printed teeth. Pitch-roll layout still has a roll-axis singularity at 90deg pitch for pointing.
